title: SharePoint: SharePoint agents in Teams mobile group chats and meetings
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents whose permissions govern answers from SharePoint agents shared in Teams, contrary to the briefing's statement that this is unknown. The roadmap facts, existing control paths and commands, licensing context, billing meter and agent-file retirement dates are supported.

claims.claim: Agents in SharePoint access organisation data like Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps, based on users' access permissions.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint access your organization's data the same way Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps does, responding to users based on their access permissions to the data.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents use sites, pages and document libraries as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint use SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries as knowledge sources to respond to the user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An agent's responses for a user depend on that user's permissions to its data sources.
claims.quote: For users who access and use an agent in SharePoint, the agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to the agent's data sources.

claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit that agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site content discovery in Copilot and removes site AI entry points, including creating agents.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or **Create pages with AI**.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change site permissions or prevent direct access to content users can already access.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whose permissions apply when several people in one chat or meeting prompt the same agent.
claims.quote: The agent responds based on the permissions of the person asking the question. When you share an agent with others, they can only access the sources for which they have permissions.
claims.fix: Replace this bullet with: 'For existing SharePoint agents shared in Teams, Microsoft says the agent responds based on the permissions of the person asking the question; sharing the agent does not automatically change permissions on its sources.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/use-no-code-agents-sharepoint/3-share-agent-microsoft-teams and add that page to sources.

claims.claim: After March 2027, .agent files stop responding and require upgrading for continued use.
claims.quote: After March 2027, .agent files will stop responding and you will have to upgrade to continue using them.

claims.claim: Existing .agent files may currently be used in Teams chats or channels.
claims.quote: You might currently use these agents in the SharePoint chat pane, through the Agent Link web part, in the agent immersive viewer, in a Microsoft Teams chat or channel, or in the Copilot app.

claims.claim: An agent can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. ... In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Licence assignment is reached at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the **Billing** > Licenses page. ... Select a product. ... On the product details page, select **Assign licenses**.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence to a user.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. ... Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.
